newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-HAYES HOMER IN NINTH LIFTS YANKEES PAST RED SOX.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-HAYES HOMER IN NINTH LIFTS YANKEES PAST RED SOX.

text.p: Charlie Hayes hit a two-run homer with one out in the ninth inning to lift the New York Yankees to a 4-2 victory over the Boston Red Sox Saturday, snapping a season-high five-game losing streak.
"We needed that win badly," said Yankees manager Joe Torre. "We had trouble scoring runs. It was just a huge game and I'm glad we got it over. We just need to relax."

In the three games since replacing the slumping Wade Boggs at third base, Hayes is just 2-for-10. His two-run blast was the first game-winning homer for New York since Darryl Strawberry hit a two-run shot on July 28 of last season.
Hayes hit a 1-2 offering from John Wasdin (0-2) over the left-centre field wall.
"I was just trying to get the good part of the bat on the ball," said Hayes. "Put the ball in play, hard up the middle. If I was trying to hit a home run, I probably would've struck out."
"He's a power hitter, Wasdin gave him his best pitch, and he hit it," said Red Sox manager Jimy Williams. "There is no second-guessing going on."

Mariano Rivera (1-1) pitched a hitless ninth in relief of starter David Cone for the win. Cone, who went eight innings for his longest stint since undergoing surgery to remove an anuerysm from his pitching arm, allowed two runs and six hits. He walked just one and struck out seven.

"I'm disappointed, I came out the best I've been all year," said Cone. "I was challenging the batters, then I got tentative. I knew we had a 2-0 lead, I decided to change my pattern, trying to throw more breaking balls."
Boston, which lost for the 15th time in its last 19 games, had its modest two-game winning streak snapped.
In Toronto, Allen Watson pitched seven scoreless innings and Darin Erstad hit an inside-the-park home run to lead the Anaheim Angels to their fourth straight victory, 3-1 over the Blue Jays.
Erstad, who was 3-for-5, led off the third with his fourth home run. He blooped a ball into shallow centre field that bounced off of Otis Nixon's knee into foul territory in left.
"You see something new every day," said Erstad. "It's crazy.
Watson (2-3) scattered four hits and two walks. The left-hander was starting for the first time in a week, having made a relief appearance on Monday.
Blue Jays starter Woody Williams (1-4) took the loss.
At Minnesota, Ron Coomer had three hits and three RBI as the Twins were helped by their Metrodome in a 7-4 victory over the Oakland Athletics.
With two men on in the fourth, Coomer lifted a fly ball to left-centre field that was lost in the roof and fell in for a two-run double, giving the Twins the lead for good at 4-3.
Mohler (0-6) gave up six runs and nine hits in 4 2/3 innings and fell to 0-13 in 20 career starts.
In Kansas City, Craig Paquette hit a solo homer and a grand slam for a season-high five RBI as the Royals ended their seven-game losing streak with an 11-5 victory over the Seattle Mariners.
The Royals' seven-game skid was their longest since they also dropped seven straight in 1991.

Randy Veres (4-0) allowed one run and three hits in 2 1/3 innings. Hipolito Pichardo allowed Paul Sorrento's homer in 1 1/3 innings but got his seventh save. Paquette homered twice off Seattle starter Jamie Moyer (4-1).
In Cleveland, Rafael Palmeiro hit a three-run homer, Mike Bordick drove in three runs and Mike Mussina won his sixth straight decision as the Baltimore Orioles defeated the Indians 8-3.
Mussina (6-1) pitched seven innings and allowed three runs and nine hits. He struck out a season-high nine and walked one. Mussina is 6-0 with a 3.79 ERA in his last nine starts.
Steve Kline (3-1) was knocked out in the second inning of his first major league start.

In Chicago, Harold Baines' single in the bottom of the seventh snapped a 6-6 tie and Albert Belle hit his 250th career home run as the White Sox got their seventh win in eight games, 8-6 over the Milwaukee Brewers.
Belle went 2-for-4, extending his hitting streak to 19 games and tying him with Seattle's Joey Cora for the longest in the majors this season.
The game saw rain delays of 29 minutes in the top of the seventh and 89 minutes in the bottom of the eighth.
Jose Valentin and John Jaha homered for the Brewers.
In Detroit, Ken Hill (3-2) allowed three runs over six innings in his first start off the disabled list and Warren Newson had three RBI to lead the Texas Rangers to an 8-4 victory over the Tigers.
